title: Incident Command Tiered Alert Broadcast
real_world_story: During an emergency hospital evacuation, directives flow through an established Incident Command System (ICS). The hospital response personnel form a tree hierarchy of N staff members (numbered 1 to N), rooted at the Incident Commander (staff ID 1). Each staff member (except the root) reports to exactly one supervisor, forming N - 1 directed supervisory links. When a code-red evacuation directive is issued, it propagates level-by-level down the hierarchy (Tier 0 is the Incident Commander, Tier 1 are their direct deputies, Tier 2 are floor wardens, etc.). Output the staff IDs level-by-level, printing each tier on a separate line with staff IDs ordered ascending within each tier.
problem_statement: Given a rooted tree of N nodes rooted at node 1 defined by N - 1 directed parent-to-child edges, perform a level-order traversal. Print the nodes at each depth level on a separate line in ascending order of node ID within that level.
task: Perform a level-by-level (Tree BFS) traversal of the supervisory tree, printing each tier on a new line with node IDs sorted ascending.
input_format:
The first line contains a single integer N, the number of personnel in the hierarchy.
The next N - 1 lines each contain two space-separated integers parent and child (1 <= parent, child <= N), representing a supervisory relationship.
output_format: Print each tier of the tree on a new line, with staff IDs separated by a single space. Within each line, staff IDs must appear in ascending order.

constraints.relationships: Tree is valid and rooted at node 1

examples.explanation: Tier 0 contains root node 1. Tier 1 contains direct children 2 and 3. Tier 2 contains children of node 2, which are 4 and 5.
The hierarchy forms a linear chain: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, resulting in 4 separate tiers with 1 staff member each.

real_world_takeaway: Tree Breadth-First Search models level-by-level communications cascades, guaranteeing coordinated emergency response broadcasting across organizational tiers.
